Maria V: seeing a surge of latency p95/p99 across inference-prod this morning, users reporting timeouts. started ~06:12 UTC. low error rate but big spikes in token latency, p99 up from ~600ms to ~2.4s. digging
InfraBot: [ALERT] gpu-mem-pressure: inference-prod-gpu-pool, 6 nodes above threshold (90% mem) - alert id: MEMPRESS-2026-0315
Jon P: any API errors besides timeouts? 4xx/5xx look ok?
Maria V: 500 rate is low. most requests succeed but take much longer. traces show blocked iterations during KV lookup + repeated cuda allocations. attaching quick heap dump and sample trace.
Alex ML: pasted the top of a worker log where the slowdown aligns:
```
[2026-03-15T06:14:33Z] model-serving-3 gpu0: alloc failed, trying fallback path
[2026-03-15T06:14:33Z] model-serving-3 kv_cache: entries=1_234_567 growth_rate=1200/min
[2026-03-15T06:14:33Z] model-serving-3 fragmentation_ratio=0.78 gpu_free=3.2GB total=24GB
[2026-03-15T06:14:34Z] model-serving-3 slow_step: kv_eviction_wait=350ms cuda_alloc_retry=2
```
Tara-SRE: fragmentation_ratio 0.78 is rough. we see OOM slowdowns where allocator spends time coalescing/freeing causing long tail latencies. KV cache growth is concerning too (1.2M entries). any recent model config changes?
Maria V: no model changes in last 24 hrs. traffic pattern shifted (more long seq requests) and a few big prompt jobs from internal test.
Kevin: allocator choice? runtime currently using default pytorch/cuda allocator + our ad-hoc kv cache in-process. big internal KV + many different sequence lengths -> fragmentation. options: switch to jemalloc/tcmalloc, reduce arena counts, or limit kv cache size and evict more aggressively.
Jon P: quick mitigations we can do now?
Tara-SRE: immediate steps I recommend:
- cap KV cache per-worker to 200k entries (env REDWOOD_KV_MAX=200000) to stop growth
- enable proactive eviction: KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.7
- restart the 6 worst nodes one-by-one (drain traffic -> restart -> verify) to defragment GPU memory and release cuda arenas
- temporarily reduce max_seq_len for the model route receiving the largest long-seq traffic
These should reduce fragmentation and tail latency quickly.
Maria V: doing cap + eviction on a canary worker now. will keep a node offline for 2 mins and restart.
InfraBot: note: automated redeploy will drain connections if you use `/infra drain <node>`
Jon P: what about enabling `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`?
Alex ML: empty_cache is not a silver bullet; it may return memory to driver but won't defragment blocks that allocator holds. it can help in some cases but slows inference when called synchronously. better to restart process if fragmentation is extreme.
Kevin: long-term we should:
- add per-worker kv_cache size metrics (bytes and entry_count) + eviction rate
- expose allocator fragmentation ratio in our observability stack (fragmentation = 1 - largest_free_block / total_free)
- experiment with `MALLOC_CONF` for jemalloc to reduce fragmentation and set decay_time to lower values
- provide a runtime flag to enable a periodic defrag pass on low-traffic windows (off by default)
Tara-SRE: for immediate canary, Maria - please run this sequence (I will be oncall and watch):
1) set REDWOOD_KV_MAX=200000 on model-serving-3 (canary)
2) set KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.7
3) reduce route config max_seq_len from 4096 -> 2048 for 10% traffic if possible
4) drain node, restart, un-drain
Command I will run for restart: 
```
/infra drain model-serving-3 && ssh root@model-serving-3 'systemctl restart redwood-runtime' && /infra undrain model-serving-3
```
Maria V: applying now. also capturing `nvidia-smi` snapshot before restart:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.105.17    Driver Version: 525.105.17    CUDA Version: 12.1   |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0  A100-SXM4-80GB      On   | 00000000:00:1B.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|    0  23469MiB / 81920MiB |  78% Default |  0%  0C  P0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Alex ML: sample trace shows repeated small allocations instead of larger pooled allocations. from allocator logs: many small free chunks causing fragmentation.
Jon P: is swapping enabled? we should not use host swap for GPU obviously, but host OOM could trigger oom-killer slowness. check dmesg.
Maria V: dmesg fine, no host OOM.
Tara-SRE: after canary results we should push a hotfix that: caps KV cache by default, exposes eviction metrics, and adds a config option to choose jemalloc. devs can test allocator change in staging first. I can make a ticket.
Kevin: small config PR idea (config names are illustrative):
- REDWOOD_KV_MAX=200000
- REDWOOD_KV_EVICT=true
- REDWOOD_ALLOCATOR=jemalloc
- REDWOOD_JEMALLOC_CONF=oversize_threshold:1,decay_time:10
We'll need to benchmark. jemalloc reduces fragmentation for many patterns. tcmalloc is also worth testing.
DeployBot: created rollout plan runbook RB-2026-0315-01, canary size 1/6 nodes then 2/6 then full. link: https://internal/redwood/runbooks/RB-2026-0315-01
Maria V: canary completed. KV cap stopped growth, fragmentation dropped to 0.46 on that node, p95 for canary route dropped from 1.8s -> 290ms.
Tara-SRE: great. start rolling restart of remaining 5 nodes with 10-min spacing. watch p99 and fragmentation metric.
Jon P: leave traces and example repro for the infra team: steps to reproduce locally:
1) spin up model runtime with small GPU (8GB emulated)
2) run a workload mixing many short + intermittent long-seq requests to grow kv cache
3) hammer with 100 concurrent clients using this curl snippet:
```bash
for i in {1..500}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>" ,"max_tokens":1024}' &
 done; wait
```
This reliably increases kv_cache and triggers allocator fragmentation in our test harness.
Alex ML: follow-up PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4212 - caps KV by default + eviction metrics + a flag to enable jemalloc. includes unit tests for eviction.
Kevin: after rollout we should schedule a benchmarking week to compare default allocator vs jemalloc vs tcmalloc under representative token distributions. I'll own the perf matrix.
Maria V: notes/actions:
- action-1: rolled canary with REDWOOD_KV_MAX & KV_EVICT enabled (done)
- action-2: rolling restart remaining nodes (in progress)
- action-3: create ticket for allocator experiment + metrics (Alex/ Kevin)
- action-4: prepare long-term fix for auto-defrag and smarter pooling (Tara)
I will update the incident ticket and close when p99 returns to baseline. :thumbsup:
Tara-SRE: adding a short postmortem template to the incident ticket describing root cause = in-process KV growth + allocator fragmentation under mixed seq workloads -> p95/p99 regression. mitigation = cap + eviction + rolling restart + allocator experiments.
Maria V: p99 trending down after restart 2/6, will keep monitoring. thanks all. :heart:
